Class ScreenPanelAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.ScreenPanelAdapter
public final class ScreenPanelAdapter extends Object
Puts a Panel on vanilla container screens. Constructing an adapter declares it; the library renders the panel and routes its input on every targeted screen, with no consumer mixin. 
Panel panel = Panel.builder("mymod:controls")
        .add(new Button(0, 0, 90, 16, Component.literal("Press"), b -> {}))
        .position(PanelPosition.region(OutsideRegion.RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP).priority(10))
        .build();
new ScreenPanelAdapter(panel).on(InventoryScreen.class);

Placement is the panel's

Where the panel sits is its PanelPosition (§0065): region(OutsideRegion) around the menu frame (extended by the screen's chrome: creative tab rows, an open recipe book), screenAnchor(InsideRegion) on the screen, center() as an overlay, or pixel(...). The adapter only says which screens it appears on. An unplaced panel, or a main() one, is rejected at construction.

Targeting

With no on(Class...), onAny(), onPlayerInventory() or onMatching(ScreenMatcher) call the panel appears on every container screen (default-on, opt-out, like ContainerPanel). Declare targeting at most once.

Frozen after init

Construct adapters from your client initializer. Construction, targeting and unregister() throw once MenuKit's declarations freeze at client start. A panel that comes and goes at runtime keeps its adapter and gates itself with Panel.visibleWhen(BooleanSupplier).

Padding

Content padding sits between the panel's outer edge and its elements. The one-argument constructor uses Panel.interiorPadding() (0 for PanelStyle.NONE, DEFAULT_PADDING otherwise).

  • Method Details

    • unregister

      public void unregister()
      Withdraws this adapter: the next screen that opens no longer shows the panel. Idempotent. A declaration like any other: throws after MenuKit's declarations froze. To hide a panel at runtime, gate it with Panel.visibleWhen(BooleanSupplier).

    • on

      @SafeVarargs public final ScreenPanelAdapter on(Class<? extends net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?>>... screenClasses)
      Narrows the panel to screens that are instances of one of screenClasses (class ancestry: ChestScreen covers modded subclasses). InventoryScreen alone is survival only; use onPlayerInventory() for the player inventory in both modes (§0055).
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if targeting was already declared, or after MenuKit's declarations froze
      IllegalArgumentException - if screenClasses is empty

    • onAny

      public ScreenPanelAdapter onAny()
      Every container screen, said explicitly. The default when nothing is declared.

    • onPlayerInventory

      public ScreenPanelAdapter onPlayerInventory()
      The player inventory in both game modes: InventoryScreen and CreativeModeInventoryScreen are siblings, so .on(InventoryScreen.class) alone silently misses creative.

      public Optional<ScreenOrigin> getOrigin(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen)
